hot100.title: Tate McRae’s ‘Housewife’ Holds No. 1 for a Third Week as Tame Impala Surges Into the Top Three
hot100.text:
Three weeks into its Daegon 100 run, Tate McRae’s “Housewife” has yet to relinquish the top position. The song holds at No. 1 on the chart dated November 7, extending its opening streak to three weeks. It is an unusually uninterrupted start: the track has spent every week of its chart life at the summit.

The clearest challenge this week comes from outside the familiar top two. Ariana Grande’s “hate that i made you love me” remains at No. 2, but Tame Impala’s “Dracula (with JENNIE)” climbs from No. 15 to No. 3. That 12-place gain is the track’s highest position across its six weeks on the chart, putting it directly behind two songs that have already established considerable staying power. Grande’s single, for example, reaches its 23rd chart week, with 13 previous weeks at No. 1.

The top 10 is otherwise marked by resilience as much as movement. Grande places two additional tracks from petal at Nos. 4 and 5, while Jão holds two songs inside the top seven. Taylor Swift’s “The Fate of Ophelia,” which has previously logged six weeks atop the chart, slides one place to No. 8 in its 48th chart week. The persistence of those older hits makes Tame Impala’s advance especially notable.

For McRae, the immediate story is straightforward: “Housewife” has kept its lead even as established favorites and a rapidly climbing challenger fill out the upper ranks. Whether its reign continues will depend on the next edition, but this week’s position already gives the song a clean three-for-three opening at No. 1.

top100Albums.title: Ariana Grande’s ‘petal’ Extends Its Albums Reign to 11 Weeks While Tame Impala Makes a Major Leap
top100Albums.text:
Ariana Grande’s petal remains the album to beat on the Daegon Top 100 Albums chart dated November 7. In its 14th week on the ranking, the set collects an 11th week at No. 1, maintaining a dominant run in which the top spot has been its most familiar address.

The numbers underline the scale of that run without telling the whole story. petal earns 71,000 units for the chart week and reaches 3,837,000 total units in the Daegon archive. Yet the more revealing contrast lies immediately below it: Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love rises from No. 3 to No. 2 in its 21st week. Rodrigo’s album previously spent three weeks at No. 1 and now returns to the runner-up position while Grande continues to lead.

The week’s sharpest top-tier momentum belongs to Tame Impala. Deadbeat rockets from No. 23 to No. 3, a new peak in its 10th chart week. Its rise is mirrored on the Daegon 100 Songs chart, where “Dracula (with JENNIE)” advances from No. 15 to No. 3. The parallel gains make Tame Impala one of the chart week’s defining developments across formats, rather than merely an isolated albums-chart climber.

Elsewhere, Anitta’s EQUILIBRIVM II leaps from No. 28 to No. 6, and Yseult’s Freak arrives at No. 7. Those entries provide the chart with a fresh set of challengers, but for now petal continues to anchor the ranking, stretching an already substantial No. 1 total while the competition beneath it changes shape.

artists.title: Ariana Grande Leads the Artist 50 Again as Tame Impala Rises 21 Places and Yseult Debuts
artists.text:
Ariana Grande retains No. 1 on the Daegon Artist 50 dated November 7, extending an exceptionally long presence on the ranking. This is her 474th chart week and her 129th week at the summit, two figures that show how much of her standing has been built over time rather than in a single release cycle.

The current week has its own catalyst: Grande’s petal spends an 11th week at No. 1 on Top 100 Albums, while “hate that i made you love me” holds at No. 2 on the Daegon 100 Songs. Together, those placements help explain why Grande remains ahead of Tate McRae, who is steady at No. 2 on the Artist 50 even as “Housewife” secures a third week atop the songs ranking.

The most striking movement comes further down the top five. Tame Impala jumps from No. 26 to No. 5, the act’s highest Artist 50 placement to date. It is a cross-chart rise: Deadbeat climbs from No. 23 to No. 3 among albums, and “Dracula (with JENNIE)” moves from No. 15 to No. 3 among songs. That combination gives the artist a stronger chart-week narrative than a single isolated leap would suggest.

Olivia Rodrigo also improves, rising from No. 7 to No. 3 as her album moves up to No. 2. Anitta advances from No. 24 to No. 9 alongside the jump of EQUILIBRIVM II, while Yseult makes a first Artist 50 appearance at No. 10 as Freak debuts at No. 7 on the albums chart.

This edition therefore tells two stories at once: Grande’s established longevity at the very top and a reshuffling of the field behind her, with Tame Impala, Rodrigo, Anitta and Yseult driving much of the week’s new movement.
